cards.text: David, king of Israel, wrote this song when he fled from his own son, Absalom. His OWN son, friend. And David skips the small talk and takes his problem straight to the LORD.

cards.question: David is on the run, and he tells the LORD how his ___ have increased.

cards.text: And it's not just how many are rising up. It's what they're saying about him. That's the group chat saying you're done for, and you're IN the group chat.

cards.question: Many are rising up against David. What are they saying about him?

cards.text: Then, BOOM, the whole song turns on one little word: "But." David stops staring at the crowd and looks at the LORD instead.

cards.question: Enemies are rising up all around David. What does David call the LORD, all around him?
With everyone saying God won't deliver him, David calls the LORD the One who lifts his head.

cards.text: So David does what you do when it's this bad. He cries aloud to the LORD.

cards.question: When David cries aloud to the LORD, the LORD stays silent.

cards.text: Now get this: David lies down and sleeps, and he wakes again, while he's on the RUN. Me? I lay awake for years in that junk drawer, and the only thing after me was dust.

cards.question: David sleeps and wakes again with enemies rising up against him. Why, according to David?

cards.text: And the enemies? David calls them myriads, set against him on every side. That's the last cookie on the tray when the whole kitchen walks in.

cards.question: Surrounded on every side, David says he will not ___ the myriads set against him.

cards.text: Then David stops describing his trouble and starts asking, and he is NOT whispering. When he gets to his enemies, he doesn't hold back.

cards.question: David cries, "Arise, O LORD!" What does he ask God to do for him?
David asks God to strike all his enemies on the jaw and break the teeth of the wicked.

cards.text: Then David wraps up the whole song with one big truth and one last prayer.

cards.question: To close his song, David says salvation belongs to the ___.
David ends his song by praying for a blessing on himself and no one else.

findings.problem: The card retells Psalm 3:1 ('how many are rising up') as well as Psalm 3:2, but it cites only Psalm 3:2. It should cite Psalm 3:1-2.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The joke 'the group chat saying you're done for' gives away the answer to card 4 ('God will not deliver him'). It also rules out both wrong answers, which are hopeful.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question sets up people 'rising up against David,' so the wrong answers 'God will bring him back' and 'God will make him stronger' aren't believable as things his foes would say. The right answer is the only one that fits enemies.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: 'With everyone saying God won't deliver him' stretches the text. Psalm 3:2 says 'Many say,' not everyone.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: 'So David does what you do when it's this bad' gives a reason for David crying aloud that Psalm 3:4 doesn't state. It also links verse 4 to the trouble in a way the text leaves open.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: 'When he gets to his enemies, he doesn't hold back' signals the answer to card 16, a true or false card about striking the enemies on the jaw and breaking their teeth. It makes 'True' the obvious pick.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.
